name: Wave Shadow
desc: A wave field solved cell by cell as a plane wavefront marches into an obstacle — it piles into standing ridges on the lit side, throws a geometric shadow behind, and then refuses to leave that shadow alone: the edges act as fresh sources and the wave curls in around them, filling the dark with diffraction fringes and lighting a bright Poisson spot dead centre in the shadow of a disc, where naive geometry insists nothing should be.

energy.doc: field gain — how far into the faint diffracted shadow the picture is pushed (master knob)

scale.doc: obstacle size against the wavelength — big obstacles throw hard shadows, small ones barely cast at all

speed.doc: source frequency and obstacle drift rate (frequency stays around 1Hz — far below anything that could read as flicker)

density.doc: wave speed (so wavelength) and aperture width — sets how many fringes fit

ripple.doc: how much live signed pressure shows over the time-averaged energy map; 0 is a pure shadow/intensity map

scene.doc: what the wave runs into: a disc (grows the Poisson-Arago spot in its own shadow), a single aperture (Huygens), two apertures (Young in the near field), a half-plane (Sommerfeld's canonical edge), a scatterer field, or a point source with no obstacle at all

seed.doc: seed — scatterer layout, drift phases, sensor grain
